Geometric memorylessness gives three explicitly verified cross-moment identities; subtracting the quadratic expectations yields the full stated deficit with all coefficients positive. The probability-space Lp embedding for p>=2 and constant-sequence equality give the exact norm; the shift resolvent gives the unrestricted comparison. Replayed rational tests match exact complete-tail sums in 600 cases. Tests do not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact sharp norm and unique equality class quantify the simplest natural geometric-weight model of a cumulative Hardy operator on the decreasing cone for all p>=2, including the p=2 boundary omitted from the motivating theorem. The explicit positive quadratic drop-kernel is a full remainder/stability identity, not merely a constant test; the cone constant is strictly separated from the known unrestricted norm. This supplies exact data absent from general comparability tests and explains how nonconstancy incurs loss.
